issues.description: HAS_PERCENTAGE regex lacks /i flag while HAS_KEYWORD has it — undocumented asymmetry.
issues.detail: In keyframe-selector-notation, HAS_KEYWORD is case-insensitive but HAS_PERCENTAGE is not. Percentages are digits so case is moot for the literal, but the inconsistency suggests the data was not examined carefully. Either normalize the flags or add a comment stating the invariant that justifies the asymmetry.

issues.description: import-notation 'url' early-return may skip diagnostics on malformed url() params.
issues.detail: The guard returns when primary is 'url' and params contain url(), assuming url-form is correct. But params may contain url() alongside malformed or mixed content the downstream walker would report on. Verify this matches actual rule semantics; the invariant 'url() present implies no diagnostic needed' is asserted, not proved.

issues.description: selectorRegex = /./ sentinel is clever where a branch would be obvious.
issues.detail: Using /./ to mean 'match everything' as a walkRules filter is the kind of cleverness that hurts readability. Cleaner: branch on whether a filter exists and call walkRules(filter, cb) or walkRules(cb). Same behavior, clearer diff for the next maintainer.

issues.description: media-feature-range /(?:min|max)-/i prefilter is a heuristic, not a semantic check.
issues.detail: The regex can match min-/max- substrings inside calc(), custom identifiers, or vendor tokens unrelated to media features. False positives only cost a parser pass (correctness preserved), so this is fine — but add a one-line comment stating the regex is a fast over-approximation so future readers do not tighten it incorrectly.

issues.description: font-weight HAS_NAMED/HAS_NUMERIC regexes have inconsistent case handling and unescaped keyword joins.
issues.detail: HAS_NAMED is case-insensitive while HAS_NUMERIC is not — pick one stance and document it. Additionally, keyword arrays are joined raw into the RegExp source; if any keyword ever contains a regex metacharacter, the pattern silently changes meaning. Add escaping or a comment asserting the precondition 'keywords are [a-z]+ only'.

issues.description: No regression tests or measured perf numbers accompany the six new fast paths.
issues.detail: The patch adds early-exit guards across six rules but adds no targeted tests pinning the regex boundaries, and the changeset cites 'performance' without before/after numbers. Existing tests are necessary but not sufficient to prove the guards never wrongly skip work. Add boundary tests per rule and record a rough measurement in the changeset.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the patch is a well-shaped set of cheap prefilters added before expensive parser walks across six *-notation rules, and lands in roughly the right form. Two substantive concerns recur: the import-notation 'url' early-return may skip diagnostics on malformed mixed params and deserves verification, and the keyframe-selector HAS_PERCENTAGE vs HAS_KEYWORD case-sensitivity asymmetry is undocumented. Taste issues — the /./ sentinel filter and inconsistent case flags in font-weight — should be cleaned up. The change is accepted as TESTED-NOT-PROVED: no new boundary tests pin the guards and no measurements back the perf claim.
